You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testJiraLang281` sets a start date at December 31, 2005, and an end date at October 6, 2006, and expects the duration formatted with "MM" (months) to return "09". The current bug report states that the DurationFormatUtils returns an incorrect value (e.g., -2).

Inspecting the relevant method `DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long,long,String)` and its underlying implementation `formatPeriod(long,long,String,boolean,TimeZone)`, it calculates the difference in time fields (milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, months, years) between start and end Calendars. It uses adjustments such as carrying over negative diff values upwards (e.g., adding 1000 milliseconds if negative, subtracting one from seconds, etc.).

For the "days" field adjustment (line 306), the current code always adds 31 days if days < 0, regardless of the actual month length. This hardcoded 31 does not accommodate varying month lengths or leap years. This is highlighted by commented notes about tricky cases for days/months difference calculation, explicitly saying it is contextual and complicated.

Furthermore, inside the adjustments, the code calls `reduceAndCorrect` to fix differences more precisely, but the initial "days < 0" adjustment still uses 31 days fixed addition.

The fix for this kind of bug typically involves replacing the hardcoded 31 days in the days adjustment with the actual number of days in the start month or accounting for correct month lengths. Because December 31 to October 6 crossing year boundaries and month lengths makes the naive addition of 31 days incorrect, leading to wrong calculations of months difference, thus returning wrong formatted months. The returned result "09" corresponds to the difference in months from December 31 to October 6 but the calculation breaks down due to incorrect day adjustments at year and month boundaries.

In summary, the root cause is in `formatPeriod` method's logic on handling negative days difference, where it always adds 31 days without calculating the month's actual length. This leads to incorrect adjustments in months calculation causing the wrong formatted output in the test case.

Recent bug reports are not related. The primary evidence comes from the failing test and the code snippet in `formatPeriod` for days adjustment.

The `reduceAndCorrect` method seems correct on its own and does not handle month length, so the bug is in how days are adjusted before calling it.

# Next step, suggest the method to be fixed.
org.apache.commons.lang.time.DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long,long,java.lang.String,boolean,java.util.TimeZone)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
